title: AIDA project file
description: The structured file at <projectPath>/project.json. Every field a script reads lives here, in one place, so the check is a schema comparison rather than a parser (02-decisions.md D6). project_state.md sits beside this file and holds what a person writes; nothing here is derived from it, and no script parses it. A field present in a real project.json but absent from this schema's `properties` is a defect in the schema, not a value to silently accept — that is why `additionalProperties` is false.

schemaVersion.description: The shape this file was written in. Repair reads format-changes.md by this number instead of inferring the old shape from what the file happens to contain (D18). Bumped only when a later change to this schema says so — never bumped for a value change inside an unchanged shape.

codePath.description: Absolute path to where the project's code lives. A project always points at code; there is no docs-only state and no permanently-unknown state (D2) — a greenfield project names where the code will go even before the directory holds anything. Asked directly at creation, one of the two facts the interview requires (D16). The check reports exit code 2, not a missing field, when this path no longer exists on disk (D18) — a producer can write a field, but nothing rewrites a codebase that moved.

frameworks.description: The stack this project is written in, e.g. ["drupal"] or ["python", "django"]. Drives every recipe and source lookup a later stage makes. Asked directly at creation, the second of the two facts the interview requires (D16); repaired by re-running that same ask on its own, never the whole interview (D4).

processRecipes.description: Which recipe each stage adopted, and where it came from. Written by the recipe-adoption sweep the first time a stage needs a cell it does not yet have (D14) — declaring is cheap and happens once; fetching the recipe body is lazy and happens when the stage actually runs. Not produced by this part; starts empty.

sources.description: Where guides, playbooks, process recipes, and agentic recipes come from, in precedence order (D10, D11, D14). The project's own source wins by default; the hosted catalog is the fallback where the project's own has nothing (D11). The project skill's create action writes this list with one entry naming the hosted catalog for every kind it offers, so a project that configures nothing still resolves. A surface for a project to add its own source and reorder precedence is not built by this part (see the schema for one `source` entry, `#/$defs/source`).

sourceOverrides.description: Per-cell departures from the default order in `sources` (D14): a team's own method for one stage, on one framework, without changing every other stage's answer. Keyed first by stage name, then by framework name (as it appears in `frameworks`); each leaf is an ordered override list in the same shape as `sources`, naming which source wins for that one stage-and-framework pair. A stage or framework with no entry here falls back to the project-wide `sources` order. Written by the recipe-adoption sweep, the same producer as `processRecipes` — not produced by this part; starts empty.

additionalProperties.description: Framework name to that stage's override list.

worktreeByDefault.description: Whether a task builds in a worktree without being asked first. Set by the project skill's create action; a project that never says otherwise defaults to false.

visualRegression.description: Whether visual regression is set up, and the path to its surface registry. Null means not set up. Baseline images stay committed inside the code repository, beside the tests that read them, never inside the project folder (D7) — this field points at the registry, never at pixel data. Written by a visual-regression setup skill, a later part; not produced by this part.

e2e.description: Whether end-to-end testing is set up. Null means not set up. Version 5 has a setup step and no field for it, so nothing could ask whether it had run (D10) — this field exists so that question is answerable. The shape past `enabled` is left open for the e2e setup skill that will write it, a later part; not produced by this part.

memoryHook.description: Whether the memory hook is installed, and which version. Memory is opt-in per project, and an installed copy can go stale silently; recording the version is what lets the check notice (D10). Written by a memory-hook install skill, a later part; not produced by this part.

agenticRecipes.description: Recipes found while researching this project's own problem, as opposed to the stack-level process recipes in `processRecipes`. Written by the research stage, updated by the review stage, read by two later stages (D10). In version 5 this lived as prose outside the field contract entirely. Item shape is not decided by this part — the research stage that first writes here settles it; starts empty.

taskRule.description: Stops work starting in this project's repository without a task. Null until the offer has been made; once made, the offer and the answer are recorded together, so a decline is never re-asked every session (D10). Version 5's block reaches further than a session, to a collaborator who clones the repository or a tool that is not Claude Code — worth knowing when this is written. Written by a task-rule offer step, a later part; not produced by this part.

key.description: Which recipe this is, identifying the stage and framework it was adopted for, e.g. "research/drupal/prior-art".

source.description: Which entry in `sources` (by its `location`) answered for this recipe (D13). The record says where the body came from instead of a verified flag, so the read-time rule for what to do with an unconfigured source lives in one place and does not get frozen into this record.

fit.description: A short free-text note on how well the recipe matched what the stage needed, written by whichever stage adopted it, e.g. "fits" or "partial". Not a fixed enum — this part does not decide the vocabulary of fit.

location.description: Where this source lives: a local folder path, a URL, or the hosted catalog's own identifier. What a location string means is decided by whatever reads it, not by this schema.

provides.description: Which of the four kinds this source supplies (D14). A source can supply more than one kind, e.g. a team folder holding both its playbooks and its process recipes.

precedence.description: Rank among sources offering the same kind; a lower number answers first. The list's own order already reads top-to-bottom — this field makes that order explicit and independent of position, so an entry can be inserted without renumbering the ones that do not compete with it.

enabled.description: Whether visual regression is set up for this project.

registryPath.description: Path to the surface registry that names which surfaces and viewports are covered, e.g. "<codePath>/.visual-review/registry.yml". Null when not yet set up. This is the registry, never the baseline images: baselines are committed inside the code, beside the tests that consume them (D7).

enabled.description: Whether end-to-end testing is set up for this project.

e2e.description: The build contract leaves this shape open past `enabled` ("{enabled, ...}") for the e2e setup skill that will extend it, a later part. Only `enabled` is fixed here.

installed.description: Whether the memory hook is installed for this project.

version.description: The installed hook's version, so staleness against the current one is a comparison rather than a guess. Null when not installed.

offered.description: Whether the task-rule offer has been made in this project. The offer and its answer are written together, so this is only ever true when `accepted` also holds a real answer.

accepted.description: Whether the offer was accepted. Meaningful only once `offered` is true.
